To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the percentage of Hispanics in New Mexico's higher education system is lower than their percentage in the general population; 2) the percentage of Hispanic students at research universities is higher than that at other types of universities, although it is still lower than their percentage among the general population; and 3) the percentage of academic staff who are Hispanics is much lower than their percentage at the general population, although it is higher than their percentage at research institutions.

the Hispanic culture is still underrepresented in U.S. research institutions, and that Hispanic students and academic staff members are underrepresented in New Mexico's higher education and research system.

the Hispanic community in New Mexico is underrepresented among students at U.S. colleges and universities and that the percentage of Hispanics among academic staff in higher education and research is also low.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the place of Hispanic cultures in the U.S. higher educational system.
the following questions: How are the educational needs and interests of Hispanic students, researchers, and academic staff members met by U.S. universities?

the question of how the modern system of higher learning and research institutions in New Mexico, the state with the highest proportion of Hispanics and Native Americans in the United States, is reflecting the sociocultural and geographical embeddedness of the state and its people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Hispanic cultures have been and still are underrepresented in U.S. research and higher education institutions.
the current system of higher education in the United States does not reflect its sociocultural diversity.
the current situation of Hispanics and Hispanic cultures in higher education and research is not satisfactory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the educational system of the United States is still largely a reflection of European culture and traditions.

the current system of higher education in the United States does not reflect the sociocultural and geographic embeddedness of its population and that the system is not adequately preparing its graduates for the future.
the educational system is not yet ready to accommodate the needs of the Hispanic community in the U.S.

Hispanics in higher education in New Mexico have not only been underrepresented but are still underrepresented.

the Hispanic community in the United States has a long way to go before it can fully participate in higher education, and that this participation is still largely dependent on the sociocultural and geographical embeddedness of the community.
